title: One approval, then unattended: light the existing auto-approval engine so Gate 2 and Gate 3 close on machine evidence by default
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a on the OWNER'S DIRECTION of the same day: "we dont want moe-next to be stuck all the time for user approval we can approve the plan at the start but thats it". An external review the same day recommended MORE human gates (preview approval required before release); the owner wants ONE — at plan/contract time — and the rest unattended, with a human ABLE to intervene but not REQUIRED.

THE ENGINE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DARK — do not let a planner build a new approval-policy subsystem. Measured 2026-09-04 (Serena memory design-710-auto-approval-exists-but-dark), re-confirm at HEAD before planning:
- packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts:157 `if (fold.optIns.some((entry) => entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier)))` is the decision.
- policy-contract.ts:24 POLICY_RISK_TIERS = ["R0","R1","R2","R3"]; :28 POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS = ["R0","R1"] — only R0/R1 may ever be automatic; R2/R3 are human-only; manual is the default; :51 no tier-bearing fact leaves computedTier null (never a silent R0). Fail-safe is the right way round.
- Also present: policy-validation.ts:181,215-217, policy-slice-digest.ts:51,54, policy-composition.ts:140-166, apps/daemon/src/http/policy-read.ts:40,45, ops-screens.tsx:157.
- DARK FOR TWO SEAMS: (1) every production caller passes `autoApprovalOptIns: []` (apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100); only fixtures carry values. (2) apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-model.ts:90 `AdvisoryRiskClass = "STANDARD"|"ELEVATED"|"RESTRICTED"` is set at new-goal-form.tsx:99 and consumed ONLY by live-goal-create.ts:50 as a line of prose. No mapping to R0..R3 exists.
- GREP TRAP: `requiresApproval|needsApproval|shouldAutoApprove` returns ZERO — the decision is spelled `fold.optIns.some(...)`. Absence of those names is not absence of the feature.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES: at the one human approval (plan/contract, Gate 1), the operator's choice becomes durable auto-approval opt-ins for preview.decide and release.decide at the tiers the policy engine permits; the risk class chosen on the goal form maps to a policy tier instead of becoming prose; the gates then close on machine evidence — the preview receipt for Gate 2, the release dossier with zero gaps for Gate 3 — with no operator keystroke. A human can still decide either gate manually, and a manual REJECT wins. R2/R3 stay human-only by the engine's own rule; this row does not widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS.

PREREQUISITE, declared in dependsOn: task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada (release dossier bound to criterion receipts at the released SHA). Auto-releasing on today's dossier would auto-release on evidence weaker than goal closure demands — the exact defect the review found. Also note task-9dbe28fdccc546dfbbbf9b32f68e7c61 (accepted node lands nothing -> checkout BLOCKED forever) is the other thing that kills an unattended run; it is an independent seam and filed separately in epic-8ebe6417.

WHO SUBMITS THE AUTOMATIC DECISION: preview.decide and release.decide are OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:378,405), human-only and MCP-excluded by deliberate rulings (comment-18dc557c, epic rail on Gate kinds). The planner must decide the principal that carries an automatic decision — the operator principal acting under a recorded opt-in is the narrowest shape already in the tree (precedent: the typed SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER arm at daemon-command-registry.ts:315-328) — and must NOT widen the MCP allowlist or let an agent seat decide a gate. The decision record must name the opt-in it acted under so a reviewer can tell an automatic approval from a human one. A malformed copy of this row (task-d4eb03f1, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: A goal created with an R0/R1-mapped risk class and an approved plan reaches a DEPLOYED preview and then a released PR with ZERO further human decisions, proven by a journey arm that asserts each gate's decision record names the durable opt-in it acted under (not merely that the outcome was ACCEPTED).
A goal mapped to R2 or R3 is NOT auto-approved at either gate: the arm asserts the gate stays pending for a human and that POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS is unchanged at ["R0","R1"].
A human REJECT on a gate wins over an opt-in: an arm records a manual REJECT then proves the automatic path does not overturn it, asserting the refusal code.

The goal form's risk class maps to a policy tier through one typed mapping (no prose line), with an arm asserting every AdvisoryRiskClass value maps to exactly one POLICY_RISK_TIER and every tier is reachable — set equality both directions.

Production composition no longer passes autoApprovalOptIns: [] unconditionally — an arm on the live dispatch payload asserts the opt-ins recorded at Gate 1 are carried; and no agent seat or MCP tool can submit a gate decision: the MCP allowlist count pins and the human-only fence tests are unchanged and green.
Auto-release consumes the criterion-bound dossier from the prerequisite row: an arm proves a dossier with a criterion gap is NOT auto-released even under an R0 opt-in, asserting the gap code.

implementationPlan.description: Add the UNATTENDED WORLD as a NEW small fixtures module beside the existing one. HARD CONSTRAINT measured at plan time: apps/daemon/src/gates-journey-fixtures.ts is 387 lines against the 400 hard per-file cap, so do NOT grow it - create apps/daemon/src/gates-unattended-fixtures.ts and re-export or import from the existing fixtures rather than duplicating the world. The module builds a journey world whose installed policy slice CARRIES auto-approval opt-ins for both gate actions, parameterised by tier so one helper serves the R0/R1, R2/R3 and gap cases. Read the two action strings from the kind constants (PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND at preview/preview-contracts.ts:43 and RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND from release/release-decide-contracts.ts) - never hand-type the literals, which drift. Respect foldSlices semantics measured at policy-composition.ts:132-170: only the LAST slice's autoApprovalOptIns are in effect, so an opt-in placed on an earlier slice silently does nothing and would make every arm below vacuous. Keep this file under 250 lines.
implementationPlan.note:
NEW apps/daemon/src/gates-unattended-fixtures.ts, 246 lines, under the 250 target. It calls journeyWorld rather than reimplementing it, so an unattended world and a human one differ only in what this module installs. Exports: unattendedWorld({design, optInTier, subjectTier}) — ONE tier-parameterised helper serving the R0/R1, R2/R3 and gap cases; installGateOptIns (one EVALUATION slice carrying BOTH gate actions, through the production policy.install command, digest DERIVED not spelled); seedGatePolicyRisk; startPreviewUnattended (drives the production preview.start handler, the seam Gate 2's auto decision hangs off); autoPreviewDecision; markPushed; releaseAutoDepsOver; onlyOutcome; releaseRunFactId.

BOTH action strings are read from the kind constants PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND and RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND — no literal is hand-typed. foldSlices semantics respected: installGateOptIns is the LAST install a world performs and it carries both actions on ONE slice, so the opt-ins are the ones foldSlices folds to and the newest EVALUATION slice both gate modules select.

TWO GATES, TWO DIFFERENT TIER MECHANISMS, and the module does not pretend otherwise. Gate 2's tier is the operator's durable readPolicyRisk classification joined on the current active graph (seedGatePolicyRisk writes one through buildPolicyRiskRecord). Gate 3's tier is the goal's planning-run tier via readRunPolicyEvaluation, which R2/R3 worlds RAISE through the slice's own riskClassifications — addressed by releaseRunFactId(world), which DERIVES `release.run_policy_tier:<runId>` from readCriterionGoal exactly as release-auto-approval.ts:209 composes it, rather than transcribing the peer test's `run-1` literal.

implementationPlan.description: DoD item 1 - the happy path. Add the UNATTENDED JOURNEY arm to apps/daemon/src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts: a goal whose risk class maps to R0 or R1, with an approved plan at Gate 1, reaches a DEPLOYED preview and then a released PR with ZERO further human decisions. Follow the file's binding house style stated in its header: read every end state back FROM THE STORE through a production reader (readPreviewDecision, readReleaseReceipt), never from the command's return value, because a DurableDecision carries no verdict and an arm on it proves only that the function returned. The arm must assert that EACH gate's persisted decision record NAMES the durable opt-in it acted under - assert the recorded action and tier field values, not merely that the outcome was APPROVE/ACCEPTED. An arm that only checks the verdict would pass identically against a human decision and would not test this row's subject.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 1 armed. New describe in gates-compose-journey.test.ts: "one approval at Gate 1, then Gates 2 and 3 close with no human", two arms.

ARM 1 (the happy path). unattendedWorld() -> startPreviewUnattended (drives the PRODUCTION preview.start handler, the seam child B wired the auto decision to) -> the persisted preview decision is read back through readPreviewDecision under previewAutoCommandId, and asserted `decision: "APPROVE"` AND `provenance` toEqual {action: PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND, tier: "R0"}. Then markPushed + ONE releaseAutoDecideOnce tick -> code RELEASED, and the RELEASED receipt is read back through readReleaseReceipt and asserted {goalId, outcome, prUrl, sha} plus `provenance` toEqual {action: RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND, tier: "R1"}. Every end state comes from a production reader, never from a return value. The arm submits NO operator decision at either gate: that absence IS the zero-human-decisions claim, and the two provenance assertions are what prove the decisions were nonetheless taken.

ARM 2 (the control that stops arm 1 being vacuous). The HUMAN journey over the same fixtures: decidePreview then decideRelease, and both persisted records assert `provenance` toBeNull. Without it, a build that stamped provenance onto every decision would pass arm 1 while proving nothing. preview-decision-record.ts:83-84 states the contract this leans on: "NULL for a human decision. A reviewer tells the two apart by this field and nothing else."

MEASURED DEFECT IN MY OWN FIXTURE, found by the first run and fixed: `readCurrentActiveGraph` answered ACTIVE_GRAPH_ABSENT in the journey world. The journey's plan approval compiles a graph (activeCompiledGraphs finds it) but leaves NO graph revision -- different projections. Without one, readPolicyRisk's fifth gate has nothing to join on, every risk record answers POLICY_RISK_SUBJECT_STALE and Gate 2's fact stays null-tier UNKNOWN, which would have made every approval arm vacuous. seedActiveGraph added to the fixtures module.

VERIFICATION, fresh: `npx vitest run --root . --config package.json --maxWorkers=2 --testTimeout=30000 src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts` -> `Test Files 1 passed (1)` / `Tests 9 passed (9)`, VITEST_EXIT=0. Nonzero executed count, not a bare exit code.

It is well under the 400 hard cap, and the sibling fixture module it sits beside is 415 lines.

implementationPlan.description: DoD item 3 - human REJECT wins. Add the arm that records a MANUAL REJECT at a gate and then proves the automatic path does not overturn it, asserting the refusal's stable code AND the layer that refused. VACUITY IS THE REAL RISK HERE: this arm is one added refusal layer away from meaningless, because a second layer can answer first and the arm stays green while no longer testing precedence - so assert WHICH layer answered, and verify non-vacuity by mutating the precedence check in the delivered production module and confirming this arm goes RED. Drill safety, binding: `git status --porcelain` the exact path first; copy it out of tree to %TEMP% with a backup name carrying THIS task id (not only the worker id, which is reused across relaunches and has held stale vintages); restore by copying the backup back; prove the restore by SHA256 equality against the pre-mutation hash in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Never use `git checkout --` or `git restore` while other rows are mid-delivery on this shared tree.
implementationPlan.note:
DoD 3 armed, three arms in "a human REJECT wins over a standing opt-in", plus a two-mutant drill proving none of them is vacuous.

GATE 2 (new coverage; the children armed this only at Gate 3). A human REJECTs through the production registry citing a node the goal actually landed (landedNodeRef reads readGoalLandingStatus, so a typo cannot masquerade as precedence). The automatic path then runs and commits NOTHING; resolveUnattendedPreview answers PREVIEW_AUTO_ALREADY_DECIDED at the layer previewAutoDecline pairs it with, with reasonCodes EMPTY — which is the arm's sharpest assertion: the engine was never consulted, so this is the daemon's own precedence check answering and not a policy verdict that could drift. The human's REJECT is re-read afterwards and is still the record.

The arm pins it on the UNATTENDED path too, where the temptation to add the fence is strongest, and asserts the released receipt still names its opt-in.

CONTROL ARM: the SAME world at the criterion-bound sha DOES auto-release, receipt provenance {release.decide, R1}. Without it the refusal arm would pass identically on a build where the opt-in matched nothing — the refusal would be "not opted in" wearing an evidence code's clothes.

MEASURED CORRECTION TO THE DoD's LETTER, found by running it rather than by reading. I first wrote both arms with an R0-capped opt-in, as DoD 6 says. implementationPlan.description: PHASE 7 - adversarial self-review before complete_task, reading the diff as an attacker rather than its author. Specifically: could any arm added here pass against a HUMAN decision as readily as an automatic one (if so it does not test this row's subject)? Does any arm assert only that an operation refused, without pinning the code and the layer? Is any arm's opt-in placed on a non-final slice, which foldSlices would silently drop and make the arm vacuous? Would a reviewer be able to distinguish an automatic approval from a human one by reading only the persisted record? Does anything here widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS, edit a roster constant, or touch the MCP allowlist - all forbidden by this row and by the 2026-09-06 governor ruling?
